questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have learned a bit of french in school, and I wanted to live in the city of lights. I have always dreamed of going to Paris and Pantheon-Sorbonne, so this was the perfect opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general information was okay to find. However, there were some difficulties with the preapproval of courses upon arrival. Further I experienced, that the deadlines for signatures provided by KU were not the same as the once provided by Pantheon Sorbonne. This caused some unnescessary stress before the semester abroad actually started.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an integration week with language courses and a welcome meeting (all in french). Further one person connected to the economics department could help with the enrollment of courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Paris is expensive and it is hard to find housing. But the Cité Universitaire is great for students, as they offer rooms for an okay price, and it is not too far from the city center. You can apply either directly to one of the national houses, or just to the whole Cité, and then they will give you a room in a random house. I applied through the danish house and ended up living in the canadian house - I found it nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not possible to live on campus in Paris, but the schools offer student housing through CROUS. When living off campus it is important to start looking for housing a soon as possible and to be aware of scam apartments. There is a lot of them in Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The economics department held a welcome meeting for all ERASMUS students, where they explained the enrollment, how to get the student ID (you needed to pick it up physically in the main building, not in the city center), and how to enroll in courses online. However something was wrong with the website, when we needed to enroll for courses (half of them were missing in the overview) and we could not reach the economics department. But we solved it, and our contactperson enrolled us manually to not courses not seen on the website. Further, the learning agreement could not be signed online, but only in pdf by the economics department.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person from the economics department - she was really sweet and helpfull. In the first couple of weeks she got a lot of emails and calls, so the response time was quite long. but throughout the semester I had a good experience with her. She was very helpfull, when I needed to change my learning agreement.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in all the classes I wanted, so that was very successfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and be pro-active. The french system is not a digital and efficient as the danish - but remember, everything will work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Without us knowing, they changed one course halfway, with a new professor and completely different subject. I did not sign up for the second half, and would have liked to continue with the first subject.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As the courses were master level and I am only in my bachelor I found some courses a bit difficult. But not too much, and I found them super interesting as well. My fellow students were also very happy to help.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only had lectures (no TD's / holdundervisning) and they were each 3 hours. It is a bit longer than KU's lectures, and i found it a bit too long. Further, we only had a few exercises in the lectures and one or two old exams, so there were not much material for studying to the exam in the end.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Topics in Environmental Economics
- International Finance
- Development Macroeconomics
- European Integration
- Industrial Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked the European Integration course. It was a bit though but very interesting. The professor is super smart, and she did small quizzes throughout the semester, which also counted in the final score. It was a nice way to always make sure, we understood what was going on. I also think, that this course had a very nice way of mixing and applying trade, micro and macro theory into some practicalities within the creation of the European Union. 

I also enjoyed the first half of Industrial Economics a lot. He provided us small exercises and I learned a lot about markets, mergers and collusion in theory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I general I was a bit surprised that Paris has almost the same price level as Copenhagen. But I did not come across any big unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is just as expensive as in Copenhagen (not coffee and croissants), and in Paris there is a different culture of going out an eating a lot. Of course, you dont have to, but I did, and it was a bit expensive. 
But museums are free for EU citizens under 26 years, which was super nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different sports you could apply for through the university. I played football with a french teams, and that was super fun. Also the university offered free french classes which I also participated in. Our french teacher took us to different museums, and she was very sweet.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would for sure recommend everyone to sign up for language courses. I did not get the ETCS for the course, so for me it was just as much a social thing, which was very fun. Also I would recommend to join a sports class, as this is one of the few ways to get in contact with the french people. But be aware, that most of the sports and cultural classes are in french.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy Paris - there is so much to see! Many museums, parks, cafes and restaurants. I went out of the city two times to travel around in France (Lyon and île d'Yeu), which was super nice, but not a must. 
Also we went to see PSG play football at Parc de Prince and we saw a Rugby game as well. Also the night life in Paris is great!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not have any problems fitting in to the local culture, I find most french people super nice an welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports team!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The french people are a bit more laid back and inefficient. It took some time to adjust to, but I learned to appreciate it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and wine culture, and how the local use the outdoor areas of the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Join the integration week and the language course. Here you will meet other exchange students and this was were I meet the people I ended up hanging with the most. 
- Be patient with the administration, they are not as efficient as in Denmark, but everything will work out in the end.
- Start looking for housing as soon as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Eventhough the french speaking can be a bit overwhelming in the beginning, it will get better throughout the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot in my courses and a lot about cultural differences within Europe from the other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses were a bit more challenging than expected, but that is probably because it was master courses, and I am in my bachelor. I found the balance between school and social life a bit challenging in the beginning as well. But in the end the exams actually went great and I have meet some amazing people and had some outstanding experiences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
